page: Microsoft Azure E48a_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on AMD EPYC 7452 processors operating at up to 3.35 GHz. Running under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor on the x86_64 architecture, this instance allocates 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU cache configuration provides 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache per core cluster. The system features 384.0 GB of system memory, maintaining an 8.0 GB per-vCPU ratio. It also includes 1288 GB of local SSD temporary storage, while hardware GPU accelerators and complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included.

Benchmark evaluations reflect solid multi-threaded throughput balanced against modest per-core performance. In stress-ng testing, single-core execution sits in the lower percentile at 760.5, while multi-core execution demonstrates solid scaling with a score of 18175.71. Geekbench testing yields a single-core score of 1352.0 and a multi-core score of 10884.0, complemented by an overall PassMark CPU score of 43071.31. Cryptographic throughput is strong, evidenced by a PassMark CPU encryption result of 46908.68, aided by hardware SHA-NI and AES extensions. In compression benchmarks, bzip3 multi-threaded decompression reaches 214.02 GB/sec, placing it in the upper quartile.

Memory and caching subsystems achieve read-only cached bandwidth of 2096.13 GB/sec for small blocks, whereas large uncached transfers register 77.81 GB/sec for reads and 38.44 GB/sec for writes. PassMark database operations benchmark at 15087.83, and Redis SET throughput reaches 38.07 million operations per second. Static web serving sustains 13.0 GB/sec. Large language model execution shows performance constraints due to the lack of AVX-512 extensions and dedicated accelerators, generating 6.54 tokens per second on medium 7B models.

Cost efficiency is driven by the density of the 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM configuration and local SSD inclusion, which minimizes overhead for memory-bound tasks. Microsoft Azure E48a_v4 is suitable for enterprise in-memory databases, large Redis or Memcached clusters, data warehousing, high-concurrency batch processing, and extensive caching layers.
description: Microsoft Azure E48a_v4 is a memory-optimized instance featuring 48 dedicated vCPUs and 24 physical cores based on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 7452 processor clocked at up to 3.35 GHz. Designed for memory-intensive workloads, it provides 384.0 GB of RAM alongside 1288 GB of local SSD storage, without integrated GPUs. Benchmark results demonstrate consistent multi-threaded compute and encryption performance, highlighted by strong results in bzip3 decompression at 214.02 GB/sec and PassMark encryption at 46908.68. Conversely, single-thread compute capabilities remain modest. Memory subsystems support uncached read bandwidth of 77.81 GB/sec, driving Redis throughput up to 38.07 million operations per second. The server offers cost-effective hardware density for memory-heavy enterprise deployments, making it a reliable fit for relational databases, in-memory caches, large-scale ETL processing, and backend analytics.
